records.supported_name_scope: The Water Survey of Canada directly names Ravn River at the western outlet of the Angijurjuk lake setting. A separately read federal fisheries report places Ravn downstream of Erichsen Lake and in the selected terminal coastal region. Continuous readable federal cartography connects those anchors with the selected upper corridor and coastal ending. The initial small feeder and several intervening waterbodies remain unnamed in this finding.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The eastern beginning approaches the upper westward trunk from the south, rather than taking its farther eastern continuation. The route bends northwest, west and southwest before entering Angijurjuk from the east. West of Angijurjuk it traverses the connected lake-and-stream corridor around Ikiqtuq, then turns south through Quartz Lake to the northern Erichsen Lake setting. Its final southeastern course reaches the northwestern Steensby Inlet shore. It does not turn south through Nina Bang Lake and Tariujaq Arm, follow the separate northern Mary River approach, or take the Neergard Lake drainage south of Erichsen. Baffin Island is the regional location, not a river-name candidate.
records.region: North-central Baffin Island, Nunavut, Canada; Angijurjuk–Quartz–Erichsen lake country draining to the northwestern Steensby Inlet coast.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence for both selected mainstem fragments using four acquired and visually inspected federal map views, retained original service metadata, directly read Water Survey station metadata and historical federal fisheries prose. The maps cover the entire eastern beginning, middle lake chain, southwestern bend and terminal coast. No substantial route interval lacks readable coverage. Small feeder names, exact through-lake centerlines and shoreline vertices are outside the representative-system question. Optional unavailable publications leave no material or access-pending gap.

naming_scope_details.selected_mainstem_sequence: Unnamed eastern south-side feeder → upper westward and southwestward river corridor → Angijurjuk and western connected lakes, including Ikiqtuq → Quartz Lake → Erichsen Lake setting → lower Ravn River coastal corridor → Steensby Inlet shoreline.
naming_scope_details.through_lake_scope: Angijurjuk, Ikiqtuq, Quartz Lake and Erichsen Lake are mapped lake identities along the generalized route, not alternative names for the river. Other small lakes are left unnamed. The route through a lake is not claimed to be a surveyed river centerline.
naming_scope_details.initial_feeder_scope: The modeled beginning selects a small southern approach to the upper trunk. No separate feeder hydronym is established, and no formal source-point claim is made.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: There are no separately selected tributary fragments. Mary River and surrounding streams are context only; they are not added to the selection.
naming_scope_details.nearby_unselected_waterbodies: Nina Bang Lake, Tariujaq Arm and Neergard Lake distinguish alternative regional drainage corridors and are not selected through-lakes.
naming_scope_details.name_evidence_limit: The acquired CBMT views supply readable geographic coverage and lake/coast labels but do not display a Ravn River text label. The river name is anchored by directly read federal hydrometric metadata and downstream federal fisheries geography, then associated with the whole selected connected corridor by map correspondence. Neither source establishes a uniform formal hydronym boundary for every upper or through-lake segment.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 328.983 km inventory value is a modeled display length, not an official Ravn River length. Fragment roles and stages do not establish an official source, naming date, current flow, exact channel position or Korean spelling.

records.supported_name_scope: Representative Umpqua receiving-system identity, with Highrock Creek, Fish Lake, Beaver Swamp, Fish Lake Creek, South Umpqua River and North Umpqua River retained in their actual component roles. The modeled ending remains within the lower estuary, short of the Pacific entrance.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The eastern selected beginning is the Highrock Creek approach to Fish Lake in the Rogue–Umpqua Divide setting, not Jackson Creek or the unselected Black Rock/Castle Rock fork headwaters. The main route continues west and southwest along South Umpqua, turns north past the Cow Creek junction, Myrtle Creek, Winston and Roseburg, joins the selected North Umpqua branch northwest of Roseburg, then follows the Umpqua bends north and west to Reedsport and the Gardiner estuary. It ends in the lower-estuary Army Hill/North Spit setting upstream of Winchester Bay and the ocean entrance; it does not continue to the offshore mouth.
records.region: Southwestern Oregon, United States; Douglas County Cascade foothills, Umpqua Valley and lower Umpqua estuary.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence of all three mainstem and one tributary fragments from readable original federal cartography, with separate upper-creek/lake and estuary enlargements. Directly read Oregon DEQ geographic prose corroborates the North/South Umpqua receiving relationship. No substantial source-coverage interval remains missing; exact generalized shoreline offsets and formal hydronym boundary vertices are not assigned.

naming_scope_details.selected_mainstem_sequence: Highrock Creek → Fish Lake/Beaver Swamp setting → Fish Lake Creek → South Umpqua River → Umpqua River → lower estuary, ending before the ocean entrance.
naming_scope_details.selected_tributary: Bounded middle/lower North Umpqua River fragment only.
naming_scope_details.headwater_exclusions: Jackson Creek, Black Rock Fork and Castle Rock Fork are distinct unselected approaches, not aliases for the actual selected eastern starting route.
naming_scope_details.terminal_limit: The complete natural river continues beyond the modeled ending to the Pacific. No extension to the offshore mouth is claimed.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Model mainstem length 328.490 km is not an official natural-river length. The map supplies geographic labels, not a formal naming decision or exact present shoreline. No Korean form is derived.

records.supported_name_scope: The generalized selection combines the Toachi direction, receiving Blanco and Esmeraldas, an eastern Blanco approach, a western Quinindé approach and a separate Guayllabamba branch. Their names are component-bounded; unresolved upstream segments remain unassigned.
records.geographic_disambiguation: This is the northwestern Ecuador system reaching the Pacific at Esmeraldas, distinct from the Santiago–Cayapas system farther northeast, the Chone coastal drainage to the west and the Guayas drainage to the south. The selected southern route approaches from the Zumbahua–Sigchos direction east of Santo Domingo; the eastern branches extend toward western Pichincha and the Guayllabamba valley. Pando is the project context, not the geographical location.
records.region: Northwestern Ecuador: Pacific-draining Esmeraldas system, with selected routes through Cotopaxi, Pichincha, Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, Manabí and Esmeraldas.
records.completion_scope: Supported receiving identity and bounded component correspondence only. This is not a completed whole-feature review. One targeted detailed sheet resolves the Sigchos valley, but substantial upper intervals remain insufficiently matched. Material pending records those actual coverage gaps. No separate scope hold is asserted; the stopped optional sources are recorded independently.

naming_scope_details.representative_receiving_system: Río Esmeraldas, bounded to its receiving-river/system role.
naming_scope_details.model_mainstem: The four fragments combine separately named Toachi, Blanco and Esmeraldas corridors; the southern initial component is not independently named here.
naming_scope_details.separate_tributaries: Seven fragments include an eastern Blanco approach, the Quinindé approach and Guayllabamba approach. No tributary automatically inherits the representative name.
naming_scope_details.lake_and_terminal_scope: The terminal context is the Esmeraldas river mouth and Pacific coast, not a lake outlet. No lake is assigned to the southern initial reach, no Laguna Quilotoa traversal is established, and no offshore estuary polygon, shoreline boundary or marine extension is inferred.
naming_scope_details.conflicting_historical_label: TPC L-26D places a Guayllabamba label along the channel near Rosa Zárate where the IGM national map and OAS river-system definition distinguish Blanco. The historical chart is used for regional corridor and coastal context, not to override that component boundary.
naming_scope_details.length_limit: 327.644 km is the rendered modeled mainstem length, not an official length of Río Esmeraldas proper.
naming_scope_details.representative_naming_limit: Distinct tributary hydronyms do not themselves prevent a representative MAIN_RIV-group name. Component boundaries are factual limitations; no additional mixed feature-class or unresolved receiving-identity obstacle was observed.

records.supported_name_scope: Río Guanipa is directly labeled on the western river corridor, the middle reach by El Cedral, and the lower channel approaching Boca Bagre. The selected coastal reach retains its river-mouth and marsh setting; surrounding delta distributaries and the gulf are not renamed as Guanipa.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route begins in the mesa west/northwest of El Tigre and north of the separate Pao and Tigre headwater corridors. It trends northeast, passes the Guanipa settlement setting, follows the river south of Aguasay and by El Cedral, then bends east and northeast past the Tonoro receiving vicinity south of Maturín. Its lower course crosses the western marsh fringe and follows the broad labeled Guanipa channel into the western Boca Bagre opening near Isla Venado, west of Pedernales. Río Amana and Río Guarapiche are farther north; Río San Juan reaches the coast separately to the northwest. Río Tigre and Morichal Largo occupy separate southern corridors, while Caño Mánamo and Caño Pedernales belong to the adjoining eastern delta-channel setting. These are geographic distinctions, not whole-system aliases.
records.region: Eastern Venezuela: Mesa de Guanipa in Anzoátegui, the Monagas plain south of Maturín, and the southern Gulf of Paria coast.
records.completion_scope: The entire one-fragment selection was compared against readable original government chart pixels on two adjacent sheets, including enlarged western headwaters, middle-course connections and the lower marsh/coastal ending. The representative Guanipa correspondence is supported without a substantial unviewed interval. The short initial feeder, exact river-source point, precise confluence and name-boundary vertices, and modern tidal/channel conditions are outside this bounded regional finding. The optional denied biological paper leaves no unresolved coverage gap.

naming_scope_details.upper_component: Western mesa headwater approach into the directly labeled Río Guanipa. No distinct initial feeder name is established.
naming_scope_details.middle_component: Named Guanipa corridor by El Cedral and onward through the Tonoro receiving vicinity; neighboring tributaries retain separate roles.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Lower Guanipa marsh-fringed channel and Boca Bagre coastal transition, west of the adjoining Mánamo/Pedernales delta network.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The inventory length is a modeled displayed-path length, not an official measured river length. Geometry simplifies bends; no precision registration, present-day channel survey, exact formal source or mouth, Korean name or language-derived alternate is established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
